e.etymology: From the English surname Hardin, a form of Harding or Harden. An old American first name, it has returned through Hardin Scott, the love interest of the After novels and films.

assoc.t: Hardin Scott of the After novels and films

e.etymology: Used mainly in Spanish-speaking families. It is most likely a phonetic Spanish spelling of the English names Katie or Kady, in the same pattern as Keyla and Keily.
The Greek and Latin form of a Persian or Bactrian name related to Persian roshan, bright. Roxana was the Bactrian wife of Alexander the Great.

e.meaning: plumeria flower in Hawaiian; also a short form of Amelia
e.etymology: In Hawaiian melia is the plumeria flower. Melia is also a short form of Amelia, and in Greek myth the Meliae were the nymphs of the ash tree.
The Russian and Ukrainian pet form of Darya (Daria), the feminine of Darius, an Old Persian royal name meaning he who holds firm the good.
The French and German form of Sabina, Latin for a woman of the Sabines, an ancient people of central Italy. St. Sabina was a Roman martyr of the 2nd century.

assoc.t: Sabine Wren of Star Wars Rebels and Ahsoka
Sabine River on the Texas-Louisiana border

e.etymology: A modern elaboration of Ella and Ellie with the -ia ending. It is also used as a spelling of Elia, an Italian and Hebrew form of Elijah, my God is Yahweh.

e.meaning: Zion, the holy hill of Jerusalem
e.etymology: A spelling of Zion with the X of Xavier and Xander. In the Bible Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and a name for the promised land; the origin of the Hebrew word is uncertain.

assoc.t: Xion, a character in the Kingdom Hearts video games

e.etymology: A modern American name with more than one source: a K spelling of Chiron, the wise centaur of Greek myth, a variant of Kyran and Kieran, or a new name in the style of Tyrone and Myron.
Used as a spelling of Cannon, an English and Irish surname, and also the English word canon, from Greek kanon, a rule: an accepted body of scripture or works, a church law, or a cathedral clergyman.

assoc.t: Canon cameras and printers
Pachelbel's Canon in D, the wedding standard
canon, the official storyline of a fictional universe

e.etymology: An X spelling of Zaiden or Zayden, one of the rhyming names built on Aidan in the 2000s alongside Jayden, Kayden and Brayden.

assoc.t: Xaden Riorson of the Fourth Wing novels (spelled Xaden)

e.etymology: A name from Mexico, used especially in the north of the country and also written Devanhi and Debany. Its origin is unclear.

assoc.t: 2022 Debanhi Escobar case in Monterrey, Mexico

e.note: Widely known from Debanhi Escobar, an 18-year-old whose 2022 death near Monterrey, Mexico drew national attention.

e.etymology: The Spanish phonetic spelling of Aidan, from Irish Aodhan, a pet form of Aodh, fire. St. Aidan was a 7th-century Irish monk who founded Lindisfarne.
A spelling of Deborah, Hebrew for bee. In the Bible Deborah is a prophetess and judge who leads Israel to victory. Debora is the usual spelling in Italian, Spanish and Portuguese.

e.meaning: fourth Greek letter; land at a river's mouth
e.etymology: The fourth letter of the Greek alphabet and, from its triangular shape, the word for the land at a river's mouth, as in the Mississippi Delta. It has been an American girl's name since the 1800s.

assoc.t: Delta Air Lines
the Mississippi Delta
Delta faucets
Delta variant of COVID-19 in 2021
Delta Dawn, 1970s country and pop hit

e.meaning: reddish-brown, from the Italian city of Siena
e.etymology: A variant of Sienna with the -anna ending. Sienna comes from the Italian city of Siena and the reddish-brown earth pigment named for it.
A spelling of Maverick, the American word for an unbranded calf and then for an independent-minded person. It comes from Texas rancher Samuel Maverick, who left his cattle unbranded.

assoc.t: Maverick, Tom Cruise's pilot in Top Gun (as Maverick)
Ford Maverick pickup truck (as Maverick)

e.etymology: From Finnish lumi, snow, a modern given name in Finland. Its sound also recalls lumen and luminous, from the Latin word for light.
The Spanish, Italian and Portuguese form of Adolf, from Old High German Adalwolf: adal, noble, and wolf.
e.note: English speakers may connect it to Adolf, Hitler's first name, though Adolfo is an ordinary name in Spanish and Italian.

e.meaning: the mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments
e.etymology: From Mount Sinai, where Moses receives the Ten Commandments in the Bible; the origin of the Hebrew place name is uncertain. As a girl's name it is most common in Spanish-speaking families, written Sinaí.

assoc.t: Mount Sinai and Egypt's Sinai Peninsula
Mount Sinai and Cedars-Sinai hospitals

e.etymology: A spelling of Amari, a modern American name used for boys and girls. Amari has been linked to several sources, among them Hebrew Amariah, God has said, without a settled origin.

e.meaning: the mainland, from the Aleut name of the region
e.etymology: From the US state. Its name comes from Aleut alaxsxaq, the mainland, literally the land that the sea breaks against.
namesakes: Alaska Young (title character of John Green's novel Looking for Alaska)

assoc.t: Alaska, the 49th US state
Alaska Airlines

e.meaning: son of the right hand, as a short form of Benjamin
e.etymology: A pet form of Benjamin (Hebrew, son of the right hand) and of Bennett and Benedict; for girls, of Bernice and Bernadette. It was often given as a full name in the early 1900s.

assoc.t: Bennie and the Jets, Elton John's 1970s hit

e.etymology: A spelling of Harmony, the English word, from Greek harmonia, a fitting together. Harmonie is also how the word is written in French and German.
A respelling of Bodhi, the Sanskrit and Pali word for awakening or enlightenment. The Buddha is said to have reached it under the Bodhi tree.

assoc.t: Bodhi, Patrick Swayze's surfer in Point Break (as Bodhi)

e.note: The Sanskrit word is spelled Bodhi, so this spelling is often taken for a mistake.

e.etymology: A spelling of Aiyana or Ayanna, modern American names. Aiyana is often said to be Native American for eternal blossom, but no source language has been identified.
A spelling of Kieran, from Irish Ciaran, little dark one, the name of several early Irish saints. It can also stand for the Indian name Kiran, Sanskrit for ray of light.
From Arabic mahdi, guided one, from the verb hada, to guide. In Islam the Mahdi is the awaited leader who will restore justice before the end of time.
A spelling of Theodora, the feminine of Theodore, from Greek theos, god, and doron, gift. The -ea- spelling follows the nickname Thea.
A Muslim name used mainly in Pakistani and Indian families. It comes through Urdu from Arabic; sources disagree on the exact root and meaning.
From Sanskrit yuvan, young or youthful, which shares an ancient root with the English word young. It is a recent favorite among Indian families.
A pet form of Melinda, an 18th-century coinage, and sometimes of Miranda. It took off as a full name in the 1970s, helped by the sitcom Mork and Mindy (1978).
namesakes: Mindy Kaling (actress and creator of The Mindy Project)
Mindy McConnell (Mork's roommate on Mork and Mindy)

assoc.t: Mindy, the human half of the sitcom Mork & Mindy
